items.h: Triple test: in a range a double top isn't enough, wait for three

items.h: Spread-out tests: the open and a bounce near overnight low count
items.desc: The three tests can be somewhat spread out; the test at the open and a bounce near the overnight low both count.

items.h: Touches a bar apart count once; open line hit 3+ times = triple test

items.h: A close-range 1-2-3 is enough; after a breakout, look at a new set
items.desc: A 1-2-3 at close range is enough; after a breakout, look at a new set. The meaning is ambiguous.

items.h: Yesterday's close as a level; an earlier touch counts toward three
items.desc: With yesterday's close as the horizontal level, an earlier touch can count toward the three.
items.src: Mixed Trading Day with Higher Close

items.h: On the big picture, several touches in a row count as one set
items.desc: When looking at the big picture, several touches in a row count as only one set. This is in a double test context and is indirect evidence.
items.src: Learn To Read A Trading Chart Without Confusing Indicators

items.h: Support and resistance are zones; three turns can span several days
items.desc: Support and resistance are read as a zone, and the three turning points can accumulate over the past few days. This is weak, indirect evidence.
items.src: How To Trade Ranges 11-22-11 Trade Example

items.h: Many bars still count as one touch; after two, wait for the third
items.src: Early Rally Then Mostly Sideways

items.h: Price goes lower in between: a double bottom, not a triple test
items.desc: If price goes lower in between, it cannot count as a triple test and is only a double bottom. The evidence is moderate to weak.
items.src: Range Day with Late Rally

items.h: Example: down day, narrow first then wide
items.desc: Down day: after the steep narrow channel breaks, price folds into a flat channel, and the wide one is only visible afterward. After the line break and a sideways move, a new channel starts.
items.src: Overnight Rally but Mostly Sideways During Regular Session   Episode 040826

items.h: Counter-example: going counter-trend with both channels intact
items.desc: The small channel and the double-layer big channel outside it are both unbroken. You cannot go counter-trend just because one old line was broken.
items.src: Overnight Rally but Mostly Sideways During Regular Session   Episode 040826

items.h: Example: down day, steep channel into a flat channel
items.desc: Down day: both the steep and the flat channel are valid. In practice, take the smaller one and use whichever works.
items.src: Pullback to the Long-Term Mid-Line - Episode 103025

items.h: Example: the big channel is confirmed only afterward
items.desc: Up day (mirror case): the big double-layer channel is valid but not useful in real time. In practice, go back to the shorter-term narrow channel.
items.src: Mixed With a Much Higher Close Today - Episode 082726

items.h: Concept: drawn narrow or wide, the break point is the same
items.desc: Sideways day: drawn narrow or wide, the close-outside break point is usually the same. A good line is touched by price on both sides back and forth, and what happens after the line break is not certain.
items.src: Overnight Sell Off Followed by Mixed Trading - Episode 081826

items.h: Concept: don't obsess over the big channel
items.desc: Sideways day: the big channel is rarely useful, and after it breaks price usually still makes a new low. Micro signals are used only with micro channels.
items.src: Overnight Sell Off Followed by Mixed Trading - Episode 081826

items.h: Concept: what to do after a close outside
items.desc: After a close outside followed by two more legs, do not chase the short and do not rush to buy the bottom. A strong trend often turns into a flatter channel and keeps going.
items.src: Mostly Sideways with a Higher Close - Episode 081926

items.h: Rule: if the decline continues, draw a new channel
items.desc: If you expected only one or two more legs down but the decline continues, admit there is a new channel and draw it.
items.src: Mostly Sideways with a Higher Close - Episode 081926

items.h: Rule: redraw if price keeps falling after a line break
items.desc: Down day: if price keeps falling past two legs after a line break, draw another new channel and watch for a larger channel.
items.src: Large Spike and Channel Down Today - Episode 111325

items.h: Example: price widens the narrow line
items.desc: Up channel (mirror case): when price keeps hugging the outer line, widen the narrow channel. Do not go counter-trend until the wide channel is broken decisively.
items.src: Two Legs Down, then Mixed and Sideways - Episode 092826

items.h: Concept: both ways of drawing are right
items.desc: Up day (mirror case): the narrow channel sits inside the wide channel and both are right. Draw it where it fits best.
items.src: Low Volume Rally Day - Episode 060226

items.h: Example: redraw a new channel after price moves out
items.desc: Up day (mirror case): when price moves out of the original channel, redraw it at the new position; the conclusion is the same however you draw it. A few single-trade comments are mixed in.
items.src: Low Volume Rally Day - Episode 060226

items.h: Example: big double-layer channel with a small inner channel
items.desc: Up day (mirror case): the big channel is broken but the inner small channel is not. Both layers are right, and the small one fits the move more closely.
items.src: Follow Through Buying Today - Episode 112425

items.h: Concept: the small channel isn't wrong, but see the big picture
items.desc: The small channel is not wrong, but there is a larger channel outside it. When price is in no-man's land, looking only at the small level is not a good setup.
items.src: Two Legs Down Followed by a Rally Back Up - Episode 051226

items.h: Concept: both layers are right, and channel health
items.desc: Up day (mirror case): the micro trend line and the big channel are both right, and a healthy channel is about 45 degrees. A single-trade entry and an EMA explanation are mixed in.
items.src: Two Legs Down Followed by a Rally Back Up - Episode 051226

items.h: Concept: channels inside channels
items.desc: A short-term channel that does not follow expectations is not necessarily drawn wrong. It may just be a micro channel inside a larger sideways channel.
items.src: Two Legs Down Followed by a Rally Back Up - Episode 051226

items.h: Lesson: where to start drawing a channel
items.desc: Range day: steep or flat, the line break is at the same place. Draw from the high along the previous two swings, and the third touch confirms it.
items.src: Mostly Mixed Trading with Down Close - Episode 121625

items.h: Lesson: how tightly a channel should fit, and narrowing it
items.desc: Range day: a good channel is one that price fits neatly. If price cannot touch either side, narrow it; weakening momentum means the channel is about to end.
items.src: Mostly Mixed Trading with Down Close - Episode 121625

items.h: Daily chart concept: the lower edge is known only after the fall
items.desc: Daily chart: in a decline, the lower edge of the channel is only known after the fall is over, and it may be wider than what is drawn now.
items.src: Mostly Mixed Trading with Down Close - Episode 121625
